Is today's mid-day meal safe, from farm to plate?

SafeServe watches every stage of the meal at Government High School, T. Bannikuppe, and sends the scraps back to the soil.

Readings

Each bar shows the safe zone in green and where today's reading sits. Food temperature is live when an ESP32 is connected; store humidity and water quality are demo readings for now.

Farm and compost

Scraps and leaves from the school kitchen go to the compost pit. The compost goes back to the farm, and the soil sensor says when to water. Soil moisture is live when the ESP32 is connected; compost readings are demo for now.

Rice, coconut and vegetables on the farm we visited. This is the soil the loop feeds.

Produce for the mid-day meal

Log what the local farm supplies, so the school can see how much of the meal is fresh and local.

Where the idea came from

We found a working farm and a school kitchen that no longer works. SafeServe joins the two, so fresh food reaches the plate safely and nothing goes to waste.

SafeServe · Design Thinking project, JAIN (Deemed-to-be University) · Safe food is served at 60 °C or above.
